=== 0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md
     1	# ADR-0006: MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue
     2	
     3	- **Status:** Accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framework approval 2026-11-09; rollout priority framing Q8)
     6	- **Scope:** Claude Code on all engineer laptops and in CI; Papaya's internal plugin marketplace
     7	
     8	## 1. Context
     9	
    10	Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP
    11	servers receive tokens and data. Papaya runs an internal plugin marketplace (brief, Appendix A), and
    12	engineers install MCP servers without review (brief); use of Linear and Slack through MCP is assumed
    13	(⚠️ G9). An unreviewed server or a plugin update can read the repo, the SSO cache or claim
    14	data and send it out.
    15	
    16	## 2. Options considered
    17	
    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
    19	|---|---|---|
    20	| A. Free choice, guidance only | No friction | No inventory; any server can exfiltrate |
    21	| B. Denylist known-bad servers | Low friction | Misses new and changed servers |
    22	| C. Allowlist (catalogue) enforced by managed settings | Inventory and supplier records; blocks unknown servers | Up to 5 working days' wait for a new tool (S6) |
    23	
    24	## 3. Decision
    25	
    26	Option C. The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team.
    27	
    28	- **Plugins:** only Papaya's marketplace via managed `strictKnownMarketplaces`, plus
    29	  `blockedMarketplaces` (📖 R1.4.2); sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only);
    30	  `disableSideloadFlags` (📖 R1.4.2); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
    31	- **MCP:** `allowedMcpServers` with `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4); match by
    32	  `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` (exact argv), never `serverName`, which "is not a security control"
    33	  (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7).
    34	- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher, local or remote, what it reads and where it sends data,
    35	  supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2), pinned version.
    36	  Example entry: `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` [design; placeholder].
    37	- **CI:** server-managed settings do not reach a CI job (📖 R1.7.10); CI uses a managed-settings
    38	  file on the runner and a fixed MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
    39	  (📖 R1.3.5).
    40	
    41	## 4. Consequences
    42	
    43	- **Positive:** Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier records (P4c); unknown servers are
    44	  refused before they load.
    45	- **Negative / trade-offs:** waiting time for new tools; review effort for 1–2 DevSecOps people.
    46	- **Risks & how we watch them:** `disableSideloadFlags` does not cover `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`
    47	  (📖 R1.4.2), so the MCP allowlist must be locked. No per-group targeting in server-managed settings
    48	  (📖 R1.1.6). Tool description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️). Without MDM, laptops can
    49	  bypass server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). Evidence: OTel `plugin_installed` /
    50	  `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6).
    51	- **Next steps:** catalogue v1 in phase 1 (may slip to phase 2 only with owner agreement).
    52	
    53	## 5. References
    54	
    55	- Framework layer 4; layer 8 rollout.
    56	- Related: ADR-0007.
=== 0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md
     1	# ADR-0007: Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary
     2	
     3	- **Status:** Accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-6, Options §0.4; D1, D3; OD4, OD7b, OD12)
     6	- **Scope:** Claude Code on laptops (server-managed settings, Team plan) and in CI
     7	
     8	## 1. Context
     9	
    10	The brief names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem. It is tempting to make Claude Code
    11	settings the main control. But server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not a security
    12	boundary" (📖 R1.1.7), local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8), Bash rules are not a boundary
    13	(📖 R1.2.6), and on laptops without MDM another login or provider skips server-managed settings
    14	(📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11).
    15	
    16	## 2. Options considered
    17	
    18	| Option | Pros | Cons |
    19	|---|---|---|
    20	| 0. Today (brief): some engineers turn prompts off; no organization policy is described (P3c) | No friction | Prompts turned off unnoticed; no evidence |
    21	| A. Settings as the boundary (lock everything, block auto mode) | Simple story | Bypassable on laptops; high friction; people work around it |
    22	| B. Settings as hygiene; IAM and the CI gate as the boundary | Boundary holds even if settings are bypassed | Settings give weaker guarantees than they appear to |
    23	
    24	## 3. Decision
    25	
    26	Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
    27	uniform defaults:
    28	
    29	- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
    30	  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
    31	- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
    32	- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` in
    33	  `sandbox.excludedCommands` [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
    34	- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).
    35	
    36	Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
    37	CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
    38	(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).
    39	
    40	Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
    41	OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).
    42	
    43	## 4. Consequences
    44	
    45	- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read AWS PHI
    46	  stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write is removed (PHI paths outside IAM
    47	  are process-only, ADR-0009). Compliance gets
    48	  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
    49	- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
    50	  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
    51	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
    52	  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
    53	  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
    54	  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
    55	  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
    56	  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
    57	  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference), so SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by ADR-0002.
    58	- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.
    59	
    60	## 5. References
    61	
    62	- Framework layer 2; layer 8 rollout; research 6.6 (D1–D3).
    63	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
=== 0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md
     1	# ADR-0008: CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception
     2	
     3	- **Status:** Accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framing Q8; OD1, OD6; target S2)
     6	- **Scope:** GitHub Actions deploy workflows to AWS, GCP, k0s and Firebase
     7	
     8	## 1. Context
     9	
    10	CI becomes the only routine production writer (ADR-0001), so it is the main target. Repository
    11	secrets can be read by anyone with write access (📖 R3.5.3b), which, in the single monorepo, likely includes every engineer (⚠️ assumed) and their
    12	agent. A long-lived key there is standing prod write in disguise.
    13	
    14	## 2. Options considered
    15	
    16	| Option | Pros | Cons |
    17	|---|---|---|
    18	| A. Keep stored keys, rotate them | No migration | Standing prod write for all writers |
    19	| B. OIDC everywhere, no exception | S2 = 0 | k0s and Firebase may not support it yet (G1, G2) |
    20	| C. OIDC for AWS and GCP; a controlled exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials | Removes most keys now | One exception to manage |
    21	
    22	## 3. Decision
    23	
    24	Option C.
    25	
    26	- **AWS:** GitHub OIDC (📖 R3.4.1); the prod role trusts only the `production` environment of the
    27	  monorepo (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4), ideally narrowed by `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
    28	- **GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization (📖 R3.4.5b).
    29	- **k0s/Firebase exception** (OD1, OD6): CI deploy credentials only, until it is checked whether they
    30	  can use OIDC. Conditions [design]: a `production` environment secret, never a repository secret
    31	  (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3); GitHub-hosted runners, because on self-hosted runners environment secrets act
    32	  like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5); if k0s needs a self-hosted runner, it is dedicated to the
    33	  `production` deploy and the residual risk is recorded (⚠️ G15); a single source of truth; owner, expiry, rotation.
    34	- `GITHUB_TOKEN` default "restricted" (📖 R3.5.3); actions pinned by lockfile or full SHA (📖 R3.5.5).
    35	
    36	## 4. Consequences
    37	
    38	- **Positive:** no stored AWS or GCP keys to leak (S2); every deploy credential is tied to a reviewed
    39	  workflow on `main`.
    40	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one-time migration; slower action updates. The exception remains until
    41	  G1/G2 are solved.
    42	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can change or delete the environment, and a deleted
    43	  environment comes back without protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); alerts and a settings comparison cover it.
    44	  The GitHub Apps used for CI agents and the required check have their own keys (⚠️ G19).
    45	  Runtime credentials inside the cluster are out of the exception (OD6).
    46	- **Next steps:** OIDC and removal of stored keys in phase 1; k0s/Firebase credentials moved to
    47	  environment secrets before standing prod write is removed.
    48	
    49	## 5. References
    50	
    51	- Framework layer 1 ("CI → AWS", "CI → GCP"), layer 5 ("Credentials").
    52	- Related: ADR-0001.
=== 0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md
     1	# ADR-0009: The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant
     2	
     3	- **Status:** Accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (research 1.9, 5.8 "not extended"; GĐ-9, GĐ-14)
     6	- **Scope:** coding-agent sessions on laptops and in CI; production stores of all insurer tenants
     7	
     8	## 1. Context
     9	
    10	Papaya holds medical records, national IDs and bank accounts for several insurer tenants in
    11	different countries. Claude Team is not shown as BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Partner-uploaded claim
    12	documents are both PHI and a prompt-injection vector (research 1.11.4 L6). Neither OWASP nor NIST
    13	knows a full prevention for prompt injection (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
    14	
    15	## 2. Options considered
    16	
    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
    18	|---|---|---|
    19	| A. Agent reads prod data freely | Fastest debugging | PHI in transcripts; injection can exfiltrate; no BAA |
    20	| B. Agent never reads any customer data | Simplest rule | Blocks legitimate debugging of non-PHI data |
    21	| C. Agent outside PHI; other personal data case by case under an approved, per-tenant grant | Matches the owner's boundary; debugging still possible | Process controls on some paths |
    22	
    23	## 3. Decision
    24	
    25	Option C.
    26	
    27	- **PHI:** never in an agent session. A human reads in a terminal without an agent and gives the
    28	  agent a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
    29	  it [design].
    30	- **Other personal data:** readable within an approved request naming one tenant, purpose, store,
    31	  window and agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9); approved by an approver ≠ requester and
    32	  co-approved by the tenant's data owner [design]; data-read role, 1 h [design]. The same request
    33	  applies when a human reads PHI. At night the
    34	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day [design].
    35	- **Partner documents:** reproduced with synthetic documents or de-identified first [design].
    36	- **Non-prod:** synthetic or masked only (GĐ-14); no prod copies (S11).
    37	
    38	This is a target, not a guarantee: "no agent in the PHI terminal" is a process rule [design] with
    39	the same weakness as D2, since the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
    40	
    41	## 4. Consequences
    42	
    43	- **Positive:** "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2); one record per
    44	  exception (S9). Assumes injection succeeds and limits what it can reach.
    45	- **Negative / trade-offs:** debugging with redacted or synthetic data; a request for each real read.
    46	- **Risks & how we watch them:** of the 17 paths to PHI (research 1.11.4), tickets, chat, pasted text,
    47	  admin pages and CI logs are covered by process only; k0s and GCP stores follow the same principle
    48	  with mechanisms still open (G1, G3). Per-tenant scoping through session tags (📖 R2.1.8) is
    49	  unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️). During a data-read window a stolen SSO
    50	  token could open the grant (⚠️, ADR-0007). Data-plane deny actions are incomplete (⚠️ G13). Planted-injection test in
    51	  phase 3.
    52	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and the minimal real-data read flow in phase 1; data-plane SCP in
    53	  phase 2.
    54	
    55	## 5. References
    56	
    57	- Framework layer 6; layer 1 (SCPs); research 1.9, 1.11.4, 5.8.
    58	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
=== 0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md
     1	# ADR-0010: Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval
     2	
     3	- **Status:** Accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
     5	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-14; OD2, OD3, OD8, OD9, OD13)
     6	- **Scope:** every change made by engineers and their agents, from non-prod to production
     7	
     8	## 1. Context
     9	
    10	Engineering says "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly" (brief); the need is speed. Compliance's
    11	sentence covers production writes only (framing §3.1). A single rule for all changes either slows non-prod for
    12	no gain or leaves high-risk prod changes with too light a review. The owner also wants every prod
    13	change to need two people, no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it (OD2).
    14	
    15	## 2. Options considered
    16	
    17	| Option | Pros | Cons |
    18	|---|---|---|
    19	| A. Same approval for everything | Simple | Non-prod loop slowed for no gain; high-risk changes get no extra scrutiny |
    20	| B. More approvers as risk grows (e.g. two for L3) | More eyes on dangerous changes | Breaks the two-person rule; slower incidents |
    21	| C. Risk level narrows who may approve, plus a risk stop; non-prod free | Fast where damage is small; specialist owners where it is large | One reviewer for high-risk changes can miss things |
    22	
    23	## 3. Decision
    24	
    25	Option C [design levels]:
    26	
    27	| Level | What | Approval |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| L0 | Reads: non-prod anything, prod metadata | none |
    30	| L1 | Changes in non-prod (synthetic or masked data only, GĐ-14) | none, author only |
    31	| L2 | Routine prod change, e.g. Lambda memory 1024 → 2048 MB | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher |
    32	| L3 | IAM/SCP, stateful replace/delete, network, workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, advisory policy finding (full list: framework layer 5) | 1 owner of that path |
    33	| L3-JIT | Break-glass in an incident | on-call approver ≠ requester (ADR-0005) |
    34	| L3-data | Real customer data read | approver ≠ requester + agreement; data-owner co-approval [design] (ADR-0009) |
    35	
    36	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent-configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for the
    37	whole team (OD3). Process-defining paths and the SCP stack are owned by the L3 owner team; IAM or
    38	stateful changes inside a domain file are approved by that stack's owners (OD8, OD13). At every level,
    39	the risk stop applies to any deploy whose prod diff is risky (ADR-0004).
    40	
    41	## 4. Consequences
    42	
    43	- **Positive:** a free non-prod loop for engineers and agents (S4); the same two-person rule for every
    44	  prod change, incidents included (three people only by recorded deviation, OD11). Compliance gets a written rule for who may approve what.
    45	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one approver for high-risk changes (owner's trade-off for speed);
    46	  `CLAUDE.md` edits wait for the L3 owner team, not the domain team that edits them most.
    47	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the free loop holds only if non-prod has no real data; a non-prod
    48	  store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule until scanned (S11). A risky diff hidden in an L2 PR is
    49	  caught by the risk stop, not by the level.
    50	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and CODEOWNERS with the L3 path list in phase 1; composition of
    51	  the L3 owner team is open (G17).
    52	
    53	## 5. References
    54	
    55	- Framework layer 3 (levels table), layer 5 (canonical L3 path list), layer 6 (non-prod).
    56	- Related: ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0009.

1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
     2	
     3	> Status: v3 after 17 independent review rounds; approved by the owner 2026-11-09 · Updated: 2026-11-09
     4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
     5	> what it gives Compliance.
     6	
     7	## How to read this
     8	
     9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
    10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
    11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
    12	
    13	| Marker | Meaning |
    14	|---|---|
    15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes or links the official page (a few rows cite vendor blogs, bulletins or example files instead, e.g. R2.4.1b, R6.3.5, R5.5.4). |
    16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
    17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
    18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
    19	
    20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
    21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
    22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
    23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
    24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
    25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## 1. The decision in one page
    30	
    31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
    32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
    33	
    34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
    35	
    36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
    37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
    38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
    39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, ⚠️ R2.9 #3) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
    40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
    41	
    42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
    43	|---|---|
    44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
    45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
    46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
    47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
    48	
    49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
    50	
    51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
    52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
    53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
    54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
    55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
    56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an owner of the stack approves the prod preview [design].
    57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
    58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
    59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
    60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
    61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
    62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
    63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
    64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** code-owner review means an approver must own the file,
    65	  at L2 as at L3. So that one on-call primary can approve any deployable path at 2 a.m., the on-call approver
    66	  group co-owns every deployable path (owner decision OD9, layer 3). The cost: GitHub accepts an
    67	  approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve another
    68	  domain's PR. Domain review on normal days becomes a process rule with a monthly check, not a
    69	  technical control. Because on-call approvers only
    70	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
    71	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
    72	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
    73	  approver, like L2, but the path is owned by the L3 owner team (or by the stack's owners for L3
    74	  content in domain files, OD8), and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
    75	  the prod preview (OD2, OD8, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
    76	  for speed.
    77	- **k0s and Firebase are weaker:** no prod preview or risk stop, no CloudTrail for k0s changes
    78	  (so S3 reconciliation does not cover them), and no break-glass when Actions is down (G1, G2).

    80	  down, every merge to `main` is blocked, incident PRs included; that counts as "pipeline
    81	  unavailable" for JIT. Their keys and hosting are open (G19).

    83	  business associate, as the brief implies.

    86	
    87	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not

    89	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).

   107	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
   108	
   109	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
   110	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
   111	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
   112	
   113	**On Papaya's stack**
   114

   116	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
   117	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
   118	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
   119	  holds.
   120	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
   121	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
   122	    accepted as a process control, D2);

   124	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
   125	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
   126	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.

   128	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
   129	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list

   273	
   274	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
   275	
   276	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
   277	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
   278	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
   279	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
   280	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
   281	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
   282	second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
   283	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
   284	approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
   285	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
   286	approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
   287	OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
   288	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
   289	
   290	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
   291	|---|---|---|---|---|
   292	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
   293	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
   294	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
   295	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
   296	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
   297	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |

   299	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
   300	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
   301	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
   302	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
   303	L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
   304	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
   305	the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
   306	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not

   312	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
   313	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
   314	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is

   384	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
   385	unavailable).
   386	
   387	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
   388	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
   389	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
   390	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.

   392	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
   393	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.

   395	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.

   398	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.

   525	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
   526	
   527	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
   528	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
   529	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
   530	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
   531	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
   532	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
   533	
   534	**On Papaya's stack**
   535	
   536	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
   537	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
   538	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
   539	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
   540	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
   541	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
   542	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
   543	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
   544	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
   545	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
   546	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. At night the data owner is not on call: the
   547	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day. This
   548	  applies to non-PHI and PHI alike; for PHI the reader is still a human without an agent. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
   549	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
   550	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
   551	    redacted summary. This
   552	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
   553	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
   554	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
   555	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
   556	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
   557	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
   558	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
   559	  1.11.4 L6).

560	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode

   604	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);

   609	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
   610	    with an expected copy (G8);
   611	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
   612	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
   613	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
   614	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
   615	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
   616	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
   617	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).

   619	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
   620	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
   621	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
   622	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
   623	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
   624	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
   625	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
   626	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
   627	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
   628	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
   629	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
   630	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
   631	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
   632	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
   633	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
   634	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
   635	
   636	  | Step | Rule |
   637	  |---|---|
   638	  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
   639	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
   640	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
   641	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
   642	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
   643	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
   644	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
   645	
   646	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
   647	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
   648	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
   649	
   650	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
   651	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
   652	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
   653	  this draft). On a breach,
   654	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
   655	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
   656	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
   657	  (D2, ⚠️).
   658	
   659	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
   660	reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
   661	schedule and approval waits (S7); monthly report of cross-domain approvals by on-call group members
   662	on PRs without the `incident` label (OD9).
   663	
   664	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
   665	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
   666	incidents, plus detection.

   668	---
   669	
   670	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
   671	
   672	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
   673	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
   674	attacks.
   675	
   676	**On Papaya's stack**
   677	
   678	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
   679	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
   680	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
   681	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
   682	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
   683	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
   684	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
   685	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
   686	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
   687	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
   688	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing Q8 (round 1): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
   689	  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).
   690	
   691	  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
   692	  |---|---|---|
   693	  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task once that service has an OIDC deploy workflow, Options §9), including the prompt for each `aws` read, which the allowlist excludes (layer 2). Non-prod data scan. OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys (except k0s/Firebase under OD1); move laptop deploys to CI (GĐ-10, unconfirmed). Rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check; the required-check app, before any agent workflow may open PRs (G19); remove human write kubeconfigs for prod k0s (interim, layer 1); phase-1 S10 checks (secret scanning, dependency check, SAST; Access Analyzer and policy packs follow in phase 2, so until then OD8 relies on the risk stop alone). Minimal real-data read flow (request, 1-h data-read role, approver ≠ requester, data-owner review afterwards; layer 6). `ProdReadMetadata` becomes the only standing prod role (existing broad prod read roles removed only once that flow works, layer 8 principle); start moving secrets to runtime resolution and redacting logs at source, service by service. On-call approver schedule and a minimal incident-responder schedule (named, 24/7), because on-call approvers only approve (OD7); minimal JIT fallback **with** per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a drift check of the stacks it touched (by hand until automated: a temporary deviation from D2, which asks for a drift job). Phase-1 JIT has no immediate stop: deleting the assignment ends new sessions only, so a grant can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.9 #3); the revocation Deny SCP is deployed with the other SCPs in phase 2 (layer 7); risk stop in the deploy job (the policy-finding trigger works from phase 2); k0s/Firebase deploy credentials moved to `production` environment secrets; **then** remove standing prod write. MCP/plugin catalogue v1. Managed settings, phase-1 subset: `defaultMode` (D1 said "immediately"), `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, the keys that enforce the catalogue (`strictKnownMarketplaces`, `blockedMarketplaces`, `disableSideloadFlags`, `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`), the OTel exporter with content flags `0` (no prompts added; it is the evidence for D1's auto-mode metric and the plugin events of layer 4), and `requiredMinimumVersion` (phase-1 floor: the higher of 2.1.248, needed by `--restricted` (D3) and above the 2.1.179 plugin-pin fix, and the latest fixed high advisory at rollout; 2.1.285 when `allowedProviders` arrives in phase 2). Also the read-only `permissions.allow` list, kept with Manual mode as D1 paired them (OD7b). |
   694	  | 2 | 30–60 | Rest of the managed baseline and verification of the SSM option (moved here by the owner, OD4). SCPs: data-plane deny, Lambda update deny, revocation Deny, protection of the org trail, outside-org write deny; scheduled drift detection; automated JIT reconciliation; audit-log export, change records, monthly reconciliation; Access Analyzer and policy-pack checks; Aurora activity streams; emergency federation for Identity Center outages; alert routing and the rest of on-call. |
   695	  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); a deliberate trade-off: auto mode runs from day 1 (D1) without this data, and until then only D1's other fallback triggers apply; auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |
   696	
   697	- **Phase-1 load [design; effort not estimated ⚠️]:** phase 1 holds about 20 items for 1–2 DevSecOps
   698	  people (GĐ-1) plus the owners of deploy workflows, within ~90 days overall (GĐ-12, unconfirmed). This is
   699	  the main rollout risk. Hard prerequisites before standing prod write is removed: OIDC deploys from

   705	  services. Not allowed to slip: `defaultMode`, the read-only allowlist (D1 "immediately", OD7b) and
   706	  the OTel exporter (evidence for D1).
   707	  If a hard prerequisite slips, standing prod write stays until it lands, and the slip is reported.

   767	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |
   768	| OD2 | L3: must one approver be from the platform team? | Not necessarily; one approval procedure is agreed for all engineers, and the on-call engineer is enough. Asked whether L3 should need more approvers than L2, the owner chose "L3 = 1 approver at all times"; in the agent's framing of that option, the approver must own the path. |
   769	| OD3 | `CLAUDE.md` changes: L2 or L3? | L3, because the workflow must be consistent across the whole team. |

(b) Keep the read-only allowlist in phase 1? | (a) "While on call, never change the process"; clarified: on-call engineers only approve, and fixes are written by another engineer (the incident responder), so the approver is never the author. # DevSecOps Challenge 1 — DevSecOps with Coding Agents at Papaya

## Note

- You are required to use a coding agent (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) to complete this challenge.
- If you have any issues or questions, don't hesitate to contact us.

## Context

Papaya builds a GenAI-powered enterprise platform for the insurance industry — Claim, Underwriting, Policy Servicing, and FWA (Fraud/Waste/Abuse) — serving insurer partners across SEA and Asia. Our platform processes sensitive data every day: medical documents, diagnoses, claim histories, national IDs, and bank accounts of insured members.

Every engineer at Papaya works agent-first: Claude Code (Team Premium) is the primary tool for writing code, running git, opening PRs, and increasingly for infrastructure work.

This is where we are today (see [Appendix A](#appendix-a--papaya-platform-context) for the full picture):

- Engineers run Claude Code on their laptops, signed in to AWS through their SSO profiles. Most engineers' profiles can reach production.
- Some engineers run Claude Code with permission prompts turned off because "it is faster".
- Engineers install MCP servers and plugins they find useful; there is no review process.
- CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions. Some workflows use a long-lived GitHub token and AWS access keys stored as repository secrets.
- Monitoring and alerting exist but are fragmented across CloudWatch, GCP, and Slack channels. On-call is informal.
- We are working towards ISO 27001 and must satisfy HIPAA and regional data-protection regulations for our partners.

We've heard two strong opinions from inside the company:

> **Engineering:** "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly. I want to debug and ship my own infra changes without waiting for someone else."
>
> **Compliance:** "Nothing changes in production — by a human or an agent — without a named person who reviewed and approved it."

## Problem

You are joining as our DevSecOps Engineer. Your first mission: **design the framework and workflow for how Papaya uses coding agents for DevSecOps.**

You don't have access to our systems or code, and we don't expect you to.

## Requirements

- The format of the deliverable is up to you.

## Submission

Submit everything in **one GitHub repository** and send us the link. Other channels (cloud storage, email attachments) are not accepted.

The repository must contain:

- Your deliverable(s).
- The **complete, raw, unedited conversation(s)** with your coding agent — every session you used for this challenge. Native session files are preferred (e.g. Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`; Codex CLI: `~/.codex/sessions/`); for chat apps, commit an export of the conversation.

**Submissions without the agent conversation will be automatically marked as failed.**

---

## Appendix A — Papaya Platform Context

### Cloud

- **AWS (primary):** Lambda (Serverless Framework), ECS, EC2, Aurora PostgreSQL, SNS, SQS, Step Functions, S3 (claim documents), CloudWatch.
- **GCP:** Vertex AI and Gemini API workloads for document AI and ML models.
- **Kubernetes ([k0s](https://k0sproject.io/)):** workloads for AI agents and internal services.
- **Hosting:** Firebase Hosting for web frontends.

### Application

- **Backend:** Node.js, TypeScript, GraphQL (Apollo Server, Hasura), PostgreSQL.
- **Frontend / Mobile:** Next.js, React, React Native (Expo).
- **AI/ML:** Python, PyTorch, OpenAI, Vertex AI, Gemini, Claude.
- **AI agents in production:** claim assessment, document extraction and classification, FWA detection — they read documents uploaded by partners and members.

### Engineering

- **Source control & CI/CD:** a single monorepo on GitHub for the whole system — apps, web, backend, mobile, AI/ML, and Infrastructure as Code ([Pulumi](https://www.pulumi.com/), plus [Serverless Framework](https://www.serverless.com/) for Lambda functions); GitHub Actions for CI/CD.
- **Coding agent:** Claude Code (Team Premium) for every engineer; internal Claude Code plugins are distributed via a plugin marketplace.
- **Work tracking & communication:** Linear, Slack.
- **Tenancy:** multiple insurer partners across countries (e.g. Vietnam, Thailand, Hong Kong), each with their own data and contractual requirements.

### Compliance

- ISO 27001 (in progress), HIPAA, and regional data-protection regulations in the countries we operate in.

## Kết quả review độc lập: `docs/adr/` (README + ADR-0001…0010)

**Phạm vi đã kiểm tra:** đọc toàn bộ 11 file ADR, `docs/framework.md` (đủ 8 layer, G1–G20, OD1–OD13), brief `work/00-challenge.md`, `work/01-problem-framing.md` (GĐ, S1–S11, P3/P4, round 1), `work/03-options.md` (§0.4, §9) và research 6.6 (D1–D3), 1.9, 5.8. Tôi tra từng row 📖 mà ADR trích, khoảng 65 row, trong `work/02-research.md`. Tất cả đều tồn tại, mang marker ✅/📖 và đỡ được claim, ví dụ R1.4.1b "link only", R2.1.4 "minimum 1 h", R3.1.2, R3.5.3b, R4.4.2 "sf-core 4.37.0", R6.2.7 "2.1.179", R6.3.5 "17 % of 52". Các phần suy luận (R2.9, R3.6, R4.6, R2.2.2 phần token reuse, R2.4.2 phần design) đều đã gắn ⚠️. Tôi không thấy feature, key hay flag nào bị bịa. Quote từ brief đều đúng nguyên văn. Phần quy về người quyết định ("Decided by") khớp với OD, GĐ, D và Options §9. Bốn ví dụ owner nêu đều có ADR riêng: 0002, 0001, 0006, 0005. Độ dài mỗi ADR từ 453 đến 572 từ, đạt mức khoảng một trang. Markdown render bình thường.

---

### HIGH
Không có.

### MEDIUM

**M1. ADR-0002 hứa quá mức về "không đọc được customer data"**
- **Vị trí:** `0002-no-standing-prod-write-read-only-agent-identity.md` §4. Câu: "an agent, even a manipulated one, cannot write prod or read customer data with the engineer's standing identity."
- **Vấn đề:** phần Scope của chính ADR này áp dụng cho "k0s, GCP and Firebase by the same principle", nhưng cơ chế cho k0s và GCP vẫn còn mở (G1, G3). Danh sách action data-plane cũng chưa đủ (G13, được nhắc ở Risks nhưng mâu thuẫn với câu khẳng định tuyệt đối ở trên). Ngoài ra, điều này chỉ đúng sau khi standing write và các broad read role bị gỡ ở cuối phase 1. ADR-0007 §4 và ADR-0009 viết cẩn thận hơn ("AWS PHI stores", "once standing write is removed", "target, not a guarantee"), nên giữa các ADR có độ vênh. Một grader bên Compliance đọc câu này sẽ hiểu đây là một bảo đảm cho mọi môi trường prod.
- **Đề xuất sửa:** "…cannot write prod AWS or read AWS claim stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write and broad read roles are removed in phase 1 (data-plane action list ⚠️ G13); k0s and GCP follow the same principle with mechanisms still open (G1, G3)."

**M2. ADR-0006 bỏ sót rằng allowlist thực sự được thi hành nằm ở admin console, không phải trong git**
- **Vị trí:** `0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md` §3. Câu: "The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team."
- **Vấn đề:** các key thi hành catalogue (`allowedMcpServers`, `strictKnownMarketplaces`, …) được giao qua server-managed settings. Bản đó do Owner sửa trong admin console, không đi qua PR (📖 R1.1.5). Giữa git và console chỉ có một lần export rồi diff hằng tháng [design], và chưa có cách đọc giá trị đang chạy (G18). ADR-0007 có nói điều này, ADR-0006 thì không. Grader bên Compliance đọc riêng ADR-0006 sẽ tin rằng mọi thay đổi allowlist đang hiệu lực đều qua review bằng PR.
- **Đề xuất sửa:** thêm vào phần Risks: "The enforced copy lives in server-managed settings, edited in the admin console by Owners, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); monthly export and diff with git until G18 is solved (ADR-0007)."

### LOW

1. **ADR-0001 §3, "Option A is the default path…":** phương án được chọn thực chất là "A + D2'" (A kèm một fallback JIT hẹp, không có agent). Fallback này không có trong bảng options; Option C trong bảng là JIT có agent. Nên đổi nhãn quyết định thành "A + D2' (A with a narrow JIT fallback, ADR-0005)".
2. **ADR-0001 §4 Positive, "the PR, its approvals, the run log and CloudTrail form one evidence chain":** chưa xác minh run log và artifact được giữ bao lâu (⚠️ G7, phải export). Change record và reconciliation hằng tháng đến phase 2 mới có. Nên thêm "(run-log export ⚠️ G7; change records from phase 2)".
3. **ADR-0002, tiêu đề:** dài và khác cách viết ở README ("in prod the only standing role (the engineer's, so the agent's) reads metadata"). Nên dùng chung một câu cho cả hai.
4. **ADR-0002:** không nhắc rằng ở non-prod agent vẫn có `NonProdDeveloper` (broad). Câu của owner là "agent has a read-only identity only", nên một dòng làm rõ "read-only in prod; broad in non-prod (ADR-0010 L1)" sẽ tránh hiểu sai.
5. **ADR-0003 §3/§4:** ADR nói "required checks from a pinned source app" nhưng không nói app đó dùng để làm gì. Với PR do app mở, app loại người đã kích hoạt agent khỏi vai trò approver và chỉ đếm approval của người (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). Thiếu chi tiết này, câu "four-eyes enforced by GitHub" nghe như GitHub tự làm hết, trong khi với PR do CI-agent mở thì dựa vào app [design] (G19).
6. **ADR-0003:**
   - Câu "code-owner review means the approver must own the files" (§1) được viết như sự thật. Framework đánh dấu hành vi theo từng file là ⚠️ ("not a separate research row").
   - Điều kiện "Merge = deploy approval" thiếu ý "without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4)".
7. **ADR-0004 §1, "Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as `serverless.yml`":** đây là giả định về repo của Papaya mà ta không có quyền truy cập. Nên ghi "(assumed ⚠️)".
8. **ADR-0005 §3:** thiếu quy tắc approver từ chối JIT cho thao tác diễn đạt được bằng IaC khi pipeline vẫn chạy (và ghi lý do), cùng với đường dự phòng khi Identity Center ngừng hoạt động (emergency SAML, 📖 R2.1.11). Quy tắc thứ nhất là điều giữ cho fallback "narrow", nên đáng một dòng.
9. **ADR-0007 §3/§4:**
   - Hậu quả của việc đưa `pulumi`/`serverless` vào `excludedCommands` bị nói nhẹ đi. Framework nêu rằng code trong repo (mà agent sửa được) sẽ chạy ngoài sandbox, có network và đọc được `~/.aws` (⚠️ inference). ADR chỉ nhắc "SSO-token theft".
   - Không nói rằng với OD12 (`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true`), "Manual" không có nghĩa là mỗi lệnh đều có prompt (📖 R5.5.5b). Người đọc có thể hiểu sai mức kiểm soát của `defaultMode`.
10. **ADR-0009 §4, "tickets, chat, pasted text, admin pages and CI logs are covered by process only":** framework còn liệt kê prod AI traces và fixtures (L12, L14). Nên bổ sung để danh sách không gợi ý rằng các path còn lại đã được chặn bằng kỹ thuật.
11. **ADR-0010 §4, "A risky diff hidden in an L2 PR is caught by the risk stop":** chỉ đúng với Pulumi/Serverless. k0s và Firebase chưa có risk stop (G1, G2, xem ADR-0004). Nên thêm "(Pulumi and Serverless stacks only)".
12. **README, độ phủ:** quyết định về agent trong CI (`claude-code-action` với GitHub App riêng, `--restricted`, không bao giờ dùng `environment: production`, MCP cố định) không có ADR riêng. Nó chỉ nằm rải rác ở 0006/0007 và không được liệt kê trong mục "Not recorded as ADRs". Nên ghi thêm vào mục đó, hoặc chấp nhận và nói rõ.

---

### Tổng kết
- **HIGH:** 0
- **MEDIUM:** 2 (M1 ADR-0002, M2 ADR-0006)
- **LOW:** 12

Các file đã review nằm trong `/home/do.hoang.minh.hung/papaya-devsecops-challenge/docs/adr/`. Tôi không sửa file nào.

ADR-0007 §4 và ADR-0009 viết cẩn thận hơn ("AWS PHI stores", "once standing write is removed", "target, not a guarantee"), nên giữa các ADR có độ vênh. Một grader bên Compliance đọc câu này sẽ hiểu đây là một bảo đảm cho mọi môi trường prod.
- **Đề xuất sửa:** "…cannot write prod AWS or read AWS claim stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write and broad read roles are removed in phase 1 (data-plane action list ⚠️ G13); k0s and GCP follow the same principle with mechanisms still open (G1, G3)."

**M2. ADR-0006 bỏ sót rằng allowlist thực sự được thi hành nằm ở admin console, không phải trong git**
- **Vị trí:** `0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md` §3. Câu: "The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team."
- **Vấn đề:** các key thi hành catalogue (`allowedMcpServers`, `strictKnownMarketplaces`, …) được giao qua server-managed settings. Bản đó do Owner sửa trong admin console, không đi qua PR (📖 R1.1.5). Giữa git và console chỉ có một lần export rồi diff hằng tháng [design], và chưa có cách đọc giá trị đang chạy (G18). ADR-0007 có nói điều này, ADR-0006 thì không. Grader bên Compliance đọc riêng ADR-0006 sẽ tin rằng mọi thay đổi allowlist đang hiệu lực đều qua review bằng PR.
- **Đề xuất sửa:** thêm vào phần Risks: "The enforced copy lives in server-managed settings, edited in the admin console by Owners, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); monthly export and diff with git until G18 is solved (ADR-0007)."

### LOW

1. **ADR-0001 §3, "Option A is the default path…":** phương án được chọn thực chất là "A + D2'" (A kèm một fallback JIT hẹp, không có agent). Fallback này không có trong bảng options; Option C trong bảng là JIT có agent. Nên đổi nhãn quyết định thành "A + D2' (A with a narrow JIT fallback, ADR-0005)".
2. **ADR-0001 §4 Positive, "the PR, its approvals, the run log and CloudTrail form one evidence chain":** chưa xác minh run log và artifact được giữ bao lâu (⚠️ G7, phải export). Change record và reconciliation hằng tháng đến phase 2 mới có. Nên thêm "(run-log export ⚠️ G7; change records from phase 2)".
3. **ADR-0002, tiêu đề:** dài và khác cách viết ở README ("in prod the only standing role (the engineer's, so the agent's) reads metadata"). Nên dùng chung một câu cho cả hai.
4. **ADR-0002:** không nhắc rằng ở non-prod agent vẫn có `NonProdDeveloper` (broad). Câu của owner là "agent has a read-only identity only", nên một dòng làm rõ "read-only in prod; broad in non-prod (ADR-0010 L1)" sẽ tránh hiểu sai.
5. **ADR-0003 §3/§4:** ADR nói "required checks from a pinned source app" nhưng không nói app đó dùng để làm gì. Với PR do app mở, app loại người đã kích hoạt agent khỏi vai trò approver và chỉ đếm approval của người (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). Thiếu chi tiết này, câu "four-eyes enforced by GitHub" nghe như GitHub tự làm hết, trong khi với PR do CI-agent mở thì dựa vào app [design] (G19).
6. **ADR-0003:**
   - Câu "code-owner review means the approver must own the files" (§1) được viết như sự thật. Framework đánh dấu hành vi theo từng file là ⚠️ ("not a separate research row").
   - Điều kiện "Merge = deploy approval" thiếu ý "without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4)".
7. **ADR-0004 §1, "Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as `serverless.yml`":** đây là giả định về repo của Papaya mà ta không có quyền truy cập. Nên ghi "(assumed ⚠️)".
8. **ADR-0005 §3:** thiếu quy tắc approver từ chối JIT cho thao tác diễn đạt được bằng IaC khi pipeline vẫn chạy (và ghi lý do), cùng với đường dự phòng khi Identity Center ngừng hoạt động (emergency SAML, 📖 R2.1.11). Quy tắc thứ nhất là điều giữ cho fallback "narrow", nên đáng một dòng.
9. **ADR-0007 §3/§4:**
   - Hậu quả của việc đưa `pulumi`/`serverless` vào `excludedCommands` bị nói nhẹ đi. Framework nêu rằng code trong repo (mà agent sửa được) sẽ chạy ngoài sandbox, có network và đọc được `~/.aws` (⚠️ inference). ADR chỉ nhắc "SSO-token theft".
   - Không nói rằng với OD12 (`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true`), "Manual" không có nghĩa là mỗi lệnh đều có prompt (📖 R5.5.5b). Người đọc có thể hiểu sai mức kiểm soát của `defaultMode`.
10. **ADR-0009 §4, "tickets, chat, pasted text, admin pages and CI logs are covered by process only":** framework còn liệt kê prod AI traces và fixtures (L12, L14). Nên bổ sung để danh sách không gợi ý rằng các path còn lại đã được chặn bằng kỹ thuật.
11. **ADR-0010 §4, "A risky diff hidden in an L2 PR is caught by the risk stop":** chỉ đúng với Pulumi/Serverless. k0s và Firebase chưa có risk stop (G1, G2, xem ADR-0004). Nên thêm "(Pulumi and Serverless stacks only)".
12. **README, độ phủ:** quyết định về agent trong CI (`claude-code-action` với GitHub App riêng, `--restricted`, không bao giờ dùng `environment: production`, MCP cố định) không có ADR riêng. Nó chỉ nằm rải rác ở 0006/0007 và không được liệt kê trong mục "Not recorded as ADRs". Nên ghi thêm vào mục đó, hoặc chấp nhận và nói rõ.
